notes: The Salesforce Platform REST API plus Bulk API 2.0 and Bulk API (1.0), authored from the vendor's own developer guides at Summer '26 / API version 67.0. 110 paths, 166 operations, 99 schemas, replacing a spec whose title read 'OpenFn focused subset' and which covered nine paths. The rewrite matters because the adaptor is not limited to its eight named operations: it also ships http.request/get/post, which reach any resource here, and bulk1/bulk2 modules for the two bulk APIs, which the old spec said outright were out of scope. Every path, method, query parameter and description comes from the Reference sections of the two guides, fetched page by page through the docs site's own JSON table of contents (212 REST pages, 32 bulk pages). Response schemas are named where a guide documents a field set - query, describe, save and upsert results, bulk JobInfo and BatchInfo, limits, list views, composite - and left as open objects with an explicit 'not enumerated' description where the reference documents a resource but never its response body; the example bodies on the docs pages are client-rendered and could not be fetched, which is the main reason this stays best-effort rather than complete. Two structural notes. Salesforce overloads /sobjects/{sObject}/{a}/{b} for three resources (external-id rows, blob download, relationship traversal) and tells them apart at runtime; OpenAPI treats path templates differing only in parameter names as the same path, so the external-id resource keeps the shape and its GET, PATCH and DELETE carry the other two readings in their descriptions, with the GET also declaring the binary blob response. And the API version is a {version} path parameter (67.0, or the alias 'latest') because the adaptor sets it per connection. Out of scope, and reachable through the same generic builders but documented in separate guides, are the Tooling, Metadata (SOAP), UI, Analytics/Reports, Chatter/Connect and Apex REST APIs. Validated with redocly lint.
